hypotheses.claim: Invalid/non-finite recurrence telemetry must be rejected before it can mint a recurrence decision.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Upstream producer validation alone is sufficient, so boundary-local validation is redundant.
evidence: Pre-fix H1 quality gate accepted negative uncertainty, negative age, NaN uncertainty and negative residual pressure into decision logic; several minted HALT_CANDIDATE_CONVERGED.
Current FRANK trajectory adapter already rejects these invalid domains, exposing cross-surface semantic drift.
H1 quality gate v0.2 rejects invalid numeric domains; 13/13 local regressions pass; 100000-case fuzz rejected all 29808 deliberately invalid samples.
hypotheses.falsifier: Demonstrate on the target H1 spine that upstream-only validation gives the same rejection, replay and recovery guarantees while boundary validation adds material cost or failure modes.

hypotheses.claim: Recurrence decision receipts should bind controller policy/threshold identity in addition to readout identity.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A fixed immutable controller implementation makes explicit policy identity unnecessary.
evidence: Pre-fix H1 gate could emit an identical receipt for the same readout under different thresholds when the categorical decision stayed the same.
The same readout hash persisted when a threshold change altered the decision, so policy reconstruction depended on out-of-band knowledge.
Current FRANK trajectory adapter already binds policy/thresholds into deterministic receipt identity.
H1 quality gate v0.2 adds policy_sha256 and receipt_sha256 with domain-separated strict hash inputs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Show that immutable content-addressed executable identity plus exact deployment provenance reconstructs the decision policy with equal reliability and lower complexity, making a separate policy hash redundant.

hypotheses.claim: Typed quality-gated adaptive recurrence will outperform tuned fixed-depth and state-delta-only stopping on real/frozen FRANK episodes under matched outcome/latency/compute/recovery cost.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A simpler fixed-budget or event-driven baseline matches or beats typed recurrence once tuned on the same episodes.
evidence: Earlier synthetic FRANK discriminators favored typed signals over delta-only control.
Residual-noise experiments show decision quality depends on estimator quality/freshness.
ACT and PonderNet provide primary research precedent for adaptive computation depth.
Recent recurrent-depth transformer research reports both depth benefits and overthinking under excess recurrence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched Golden Trace benchmark where a simpler controller equals/exceeds typed recurrence on correctness, false convergence, overthinking, latency, compute and recovery.

hypotheses.claim: The future fused H1 recurrence receipt should bind state-ledger version/trace identity, not only state_epoch and a local readout hash, when that integration is available.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: state_epoch plus readout/policy/receipt hashes is sufficient because ledger lineage can always be recovered externally.
evidence: H-WP-02 oracle ledger already distinguishes semantic_state_hash, state_version_hash and trace_root_hash.
OpenTelemetry/W3C provenance models preserve causal/trace identity separately from payload state.
Current quality-gate v0.2 closes local policy identity but does not yet carry H-WP-02 state-version/trace roots.
hypotheses.falsifier: Replay/differential tests show no ambiguity or recovery/audit benefit from direct state-version/trace binding across stale, duplicate, crash-recovery and cross-instance cases.

hypotheses.claim: Residual uncertainty/freshness and convergence thresholds should be calibrated and versioned per estimator/loop family rather than frozen globally without trace evidence.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One global threshold set is robust enough across FRANK loop families and estimators.
evidence: Synthetic sensitivity work showed false convergence changes materially with residual measurement noise/staleness.
Current hard thresholds are engineering defaults, not target-trace-calibrated measurements.
Adaptive-computation literature indicates useful stopping depth is task/input dependent.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target/frozen H1 benchmarks show global thresholds remain calibrated across estimator versions, loop families and OOD episodes with no material loss versus per-family calibration.
